newsitem.title: USA: Posthumous Shakur album jumps to top of U.S. chart.
newsitem.headline: Posthumous Shakur album jumps to top of U.S. chart.

text.p: Two months after his death, gangsta rapper Tupac Shakur returned to the top of the U.S. album charts with record first-week sales, his label said on Wednesday.

The album, "The Don Killuminati -- the 7 Day Theory," which Shakur recorded under the alter ego Makaveli, sold almost 664,000 copies in the week ended November 10, more than three times as many as the number two album.
Shakur was gunned down in an unsolved drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on September 7 and died six days later.

During his brief recording career, the 25-year-old spent time in prison for sexual assault and was criticized for the hard-core nature of his songs. His acting turns in such movies as "Poetic Justice" and "Above The Rim" won favorable reviews.

His previous release, the double album "All Eyez On Me," opened with 565,500 copies in February 1996. First-week sales for "Me Against the World," his third solo album, were 210,000 in March 1995. Each spent two weeks at number one.
The album, distributed by Sony Corp's Relativity Records, sold almost 219,000 copies, Mo Thugs said. The label was formed by the members of chart-topping rappers Bone Thugs-N- Harmony.
Sony also took third place with Celine Dion, whose "Falling Into You" sold over 126,000 copies, up from 122,000 the week before when it was fifth. Dion records for Sony's Epic Records label.
